unresolved_added: The source coefficient regressions have no data table, estimation method, fit diagnostics, units, or uncertainty, and their error terms are not propagated.
The literature claims use a small reference set and cannot establish that no prior size-specific work existed.
Balanced AOI/OA exchange and geography factors lambda_1 and lambda_2 are assumed without calibration or a mass-conserving transport model.
The prose says physical abrasion removes a proportion of initial size, while Equation (4) makes loss proportional to current S(t).
Physical and chemical loss are added as constant first-order rates without evidence that the mechanisms share one scale or remain constant.
The half-life interpretation is used as if photolysis alone identifies r_2, although the preceding trajectory contains both r_1 and r_2.
The four size classes are engineered from an exponential ratio and food-size analogy rather than validated ecological exposure classes.
Equation (6) and the transition-time argument assume all particles cross a class boundary together and preserve a single deterministic size.
The compartment equations mix whole-object transfer, physical fragments, chemical products, and concentration inputs without a fully typed mass basis.
Physical abrasion simultaneously removes material and contributes it to Level 3, while chemical loss contributes to Level 4; conservation and double counting are not demonstrated.
The system balance depends on cancellation of printed terms, but the units and treatment of harmless chemical products are not closed.
Equations (13)-(16) are presented as solutions while C_1, C_2, and C_3 still appear on right-hand sides; direct substitution does not establish solutions of the coupled ODE system.
The forcing solution for Equation (8) should generally contain a rate-dependent steady contribution rather than only I_1 t plus a decaying initial term.
The paper infers C_20=10 from a 5.1 kg/km2 observation by a rough half-range argument, then sets all four initial concentrations equal without data.
Level-4 toxicity is dismissed using a rough mass comparison even though the paper later admits low-concentration molecular toxicity may matter.
The text moves from r_2=1 percent to r_1=r_2 and then r_2=6.9 percent without a coherent derivation of both rates.
The chosen m=100 years is not reconciled with m=ln(10^6)/(r_1+r_2) across the stated rate range.
Figures 2-4 are internally generated curves with no released code, parameter file, uncertainty band, or observed concentration validation.
The claimed input threshold for continuous decline is described qualitatively but never solved or reported numerically.
The D1-D3 input distributions are a narrow hand-picked set; calling one optimized is unsupported by an optimization problem or exhaustive search.
The treatment recommendation does not model treatment cost, feasibility, byproducts, compliance, or effects on input mass.
Physical abrasion is set equal to photolysis despite the source itself describing abrasion as difficult to predict.
Equation (19) equates a first-order rate term and photon-yield term without documenting units, concentration basis, or polymer-specific calibration.
Equation (20) omits integration/bandwidth details and uses no site-specific spectral data, latitude series, cloud cover, depth, or mixing.
The comparison expands r_2 to 15 percent although the earlier estimated range is 1-6.9 percent, justified only by possible technology advancement.
The 30-year comparison point is selected from a visual transient rather than a decision horizon or validated ecological response time.
The derivative rankings are asserted from plotted surfaces without an analytic derivative, units, sign convention, or numerical table.
Equation (23) is an equality of marginal influences, not a dynamical equilibrium; the label equilibrium point overstates its meaning.
The proposed long-run repair f(t) is not specified, fitted, simulated, or compared with the original linear input.
The model is bounded to 30-50 years only rhetorically; no horizon-specific validation demonstrates adequacy over that interval.
Calling Level-3 concentration an ecosystem indicator is not validated against organism exposure, abundance, health, or ecological balance.
Taxes, mandatory treatment, cleanup, and material restrictions are recommended without causal effects, costs, enforcement, equity, or stakeholder analysis.
Plastic quality is redefined as photolysis rate, which can conflict with durability, toxicity, fragmentation, and life-cycle environmental quality.
The recommendation to encourage easily degradable plastics when quality is low ignores whether faster fragmentation increases microplastic or molecular exposure.
The paper provides no executable model, raw data, parameter manifest, solver log, or independent test set, so all numerical figures remain non-reproducible.
Table and equation cross-references drift: the text calls the size-category table Table 1 after it is captioned Table 2.
